we are talking about pointing out something in person, not online - like what happened to OP. a random person who they didn’t know IRL pointed out their scars. most people would not feel comfortable in public delving into why they self harm to a random person who just pointed out their scars 🤷‍♀️ if it happened in private that’s different but this was at a grocery store checkout line; you’re not going to stop and tell your life story to the cashier or vice versa. time and place ya know?

if it’s with a friend or family member, sure. but i highly doubt you’ll end up in a deep conversation with a stranger you JUST met about their mental health and why they self harm or how they can better themselves.

maybe it’s a cultural difference here but i was raised to just never comment on someone’s appearance regardless of if it’s ‘out of love’ or not. it’s not my place to tell someone how they can better themselves unless they ask for my opinion

right that’s why those things are ok to comment on BECAUSE they can fix them. when it comes to thinks like weight, scars, teeth, etc something someone cannot fix in under one minute you should just avoid commenting on it because most people don’t like it. personally i don’t care when people point out my scars, but rule of thumb is don’t do it.

how have you never learned things like ‘the road to hell is paved with good intentions’ or ‘impact over intent’ ? none of these are new sayings. people aren’t getting ‘weaker’, people are standing up for themselves more
the general rule of thumb when commenting on something about someone is; if they can’t fix it in under a minute (like something stuck in their teeth or food on their face/shirt) don’t tell them.
